from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Language of Sine Waves", [
            "Sine waves defined by amplitude, frequency, phase.",
            "View sine waves as rotating vectors, phasors.",
            "Add waves together using the Superposition Principle."
        ])
        
        # Pre-render objects
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x * 2), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00CED1")
        peak = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(wave.point_from_proportion(0.25))
        trough = Dot(color=RED).move_to(wave.point_from_proportion(0.75))
        label_peak = Text("Peak", font_size=18, color=YELLOW).next_to(peak, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_trough = Text("Trough", font_size=18, color=RED).next_to(trough, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.place_in_area(wave, "A1", "C6")
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(peak), FadeIn(trough), Write(label_peak), Write(label_trough))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        # Animate wave oscillation
        freq = ValueTracker(2)
        wave.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x * freq.get_value()), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00CED1")
        ))
        self.play(freq.animate.set_value(4), run_time=2)
        self.play(freq.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        wave.remove_updater(wave.updaters[0])
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: The Rotating Windmill", [
            "Fourier Transform acts as a mathematical sieve.", 
            "Multiply signal by complex rotating exponentials.", 
            "Align rotation speed with signal frequency.", 
            "Constructive interference creates spectrum peaks.", 
            "Shift center of gravity reveals components."
        ])
        
        # Setup Animation Objects
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=GRAY)
        arm = Line(ORIGIN, 1.5 * RIGHT, color="#FFA500")
        tip = Dot(arm.get_end(), color="#FFA500")
        shadow = Dot(np.array([1.5, 0, 0]), color=BLUE) # Projection on Y axis
        
        windmill = VGroup(circle, arm, tip)
        self.place_at_grid(windmill, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(shadow, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Update trackers
        angle = ValueTracker(0)
        arm.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(circle.get_center(), circle.get_center() + 1.5 * np.array([np.cos(angle.get_value()), np.sin(angle.get_value()), 0])))
        tip.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(arm.get_end()))
        shadow.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(np.array([circle.get_center()[0] + 1.5, circle.get_center()[1] + 1.5 * np.sin(angle.get_value()), 0])))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(windmill), FadeIn(shadow))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(2*PI), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(4*PI), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(6*PI), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(8*PI), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFA500")

        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Real-World Application", [
            "Transformations allow us to manipulate signals.",
            "Remove hiss or compress images easily.",
            "Everything is just a sum of vibrations."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        waveform = FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(2 * np.pi * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * np.pi * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        spectrum = BarChart(values=[5, 8, 3, 1, 0.5], bar_colors=[BLUE, BLUE, BLUE, BLUE, BLUE])
        audio_label = Text("Audio Analysis", color="#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(waveform, 'B3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(waveform))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(waveform, spectrum))
        self.place_at_grid(spectrum, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(audio_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(audio_label))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Introduction: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be deconstructed back into its original fruit ingredients (strawberries, bananas, blueberries), a complex signal can be broken down into simple sine waves. Define the core objective: transforming data from the Time Domain to the Frequency Domain.
sections.example: A chef blending fruits to create a smoothie; the Fourier Transform acts as the 'inverse blender' that tells you exactly how many grams of each fruit were used.

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Sine Waves (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: Briefly review the parameters of a sine wave: Amplitude, Frequency, and Phase. Visualize these as rotating vectors (phasors) on a complex plane. This builds the foundational mental model for adding multiple waves together to create complex patterns (Superposition Principle).
sections.example: A visual animation showing three simple sine waves of different frequencies stacking up to form a complex 'sawtooth' wave.

sections.title: The Core Concept: The Rotating Windmill (1:45-3:15)
sections.content: Explain the Fourier Transform as a mathematical 'sieve'. We multiply the signal by complex exponentials (rotating vectors) at different frequencies. When the 'rotation speed' matches a frequency hidden in the signal, the signal 'aligns' (constructive interference), creating a peak in the spectrum.
sections.example: An animation of a 'spirograph' drawing: The signal wraps around a center point. If the winding frequency matches the signal frequency, the center of gravity shifts away from the origin, revealing the hidden component.

sections.title: The Result: The Frequency Spectrum (3:15-4:15)
sections.content: Explain the transition from a wave-form (Time Domain) to a 'Bar Chart' (Frequency Domain). Discuss how the peaks in the spectrum represent the 'DNA' of the signal, allowing us to filter noise or compress files.
sections.example: An audio signal of a cat meowing. Show the messy wave in the time domain, then animate it snapping into a neat set of distinct bars on a frequency plot.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-World Application (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Summarize how this transformation allows us to manipulate signals—like removing high-frequency hiss from old recordings or compressing images (JPEG). End with the 'big picture': Everything in the universe is just a sum of vibrations.
sections.example: A smartphone using Fourier Transform to perform 'Shazam'—identifying a song by matching its unique frequency fingerprint against a database.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The blender animation (C3) is visually competing with the lecture text, reducing readability and balance. Fix: Line 64: self.place_at_grid('blender', 'D4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=64, object=blender)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Ingredients (strawberry and banana) are clustered too close to the upper-left, causing visual imbalance with the right-side grid. Fix: Line 66: self.place_at_grid('strawberry', 'D2', scale_factor=0.6); Line 67: self.place_at_grid('banana', 'D6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=66, object=strawberry, banana)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The resulting smoothie object is centered in the same location as the blender, creating redundant layering and potential occlusion. Fix: Line 84: self.place_at_grid('smoothie', 'E4', scale_factor=0.8) (line=84, object=smoothie)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The sine wave animation occupies a large area (A1-C6), causing it to collide visually with the left-aligned lecture text. Fix: self.place_in_area(wave, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=62, object=wave)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Labels 'Peak' and 'Trough' are placed too far from their respective extrema, creating visual clutter across the grid. Fix: self.place_at_grid(peak_label, 'D1', scale_factor=0.5); self.place_at_grid(trough_label, 'F1', scale_factor=0.5) (line=63, object=labels)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The visual elements lack vertical breathing room, creating a cramped layout in the upper-right quadrant. Fix: self.place_in_area(wave, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=64, object=wave)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The rotating windmill and its shadow are too close to the left-hand lecture text, creating visual clutter and potential obstruction. Fix: Line 63: self.place_at_grid('windmill', 'C3', scale_factor=0.8); Line 64: self.place_at_grid('shadow', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=63, object=windmill and shadow)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Poor grid utilization; objects are clustered in row B, leaving the bottom half of the right-side workspace empty. Fix: Line 63: self.place_at_grid('windmill', 'D2', scale_factor=0.9); Line 64: self.place_at_grid('shadow', 'D5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=63, object=windmill and shadow)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Scale factor 0.8 is too small for the available 6x6 grid area, causing the animation to appear detached from the instructional flow. Fix: Line 63: self.place_in_area('windmill', 'C2', 'D3', scale_factor=1.2); Line 64: self.place_in_area('shadow', 'C4', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2) (line=63, object=windmill and shadow)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The bar chart occupies a large 4x6 area (B1-E6) causing crowding and poor visual balance on the right side. Fix: self.place_in_area(bar_chart, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=1, object=bar_chart)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The tight cluster of the chart against the edges reduces the overall aesthetic and creates unnecessary visual tension. Fix: self.place_at_grid(bar_chart, 'C4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=2, object=bar_chart)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The current scale (0.8) is too large for the allocated grid, risking overlap with future animated elements. Fix: self.place_in_area(bar_chart, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.55) (line=3, object=bar_chart)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Audio Analysis label is cramped and poorly aligned with the chart. Fix: Line 74: self.place_at_grid(audio_label, 'A4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=74, object=audio_label)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The waveform visual overlaps with the spectrum chart in the vertical axis. Fix: Line 60: self.place_at_grid(waveform, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6) (line=60, object=waveform)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The spectrum chart is vertically constrained by the waveform, reducing clarity. Fix: Line 68: self.place_at_grid(spectrum, 'C2', scale_factor=0.7) (line=68, object=spectrum)
